lesson_title: The Poster on the Restaurant Wall
hook_text: Every workplace in South Africa must have a poster on the wall. Most workers have never read it. Here is what it promises you.
clip_script: Friday night at a restaurant. The dishwasher learned his job in an afternoon: unskilled. The waiters had some training: semi-skilled. The chef studied for years: skilled. Different skills, different pay. But all of them are protected by the poster in the back passage. Forty-five ordinary hours a week, maximum. Extra hours? Overtime at one and a half times: a forty-rand-an-hour waiter gets sixty for every extra hour. Nobody below the national minimum wage: twenty-eight rand seventy-nine an hour. Paid leave, sick leave, four months' maternity leave. A payslip. No discrimination. A fair hearing before anyone is fired, and the CCMA if there is a dispute. Fair rules are not just kind. Happy workers stay, and they treat the customers better.
visual_style: A whiteboard restaurant cross-section with three workers labelled unskilled, semi-skilled and skilled, then a wall poster with ticks appearing next to each right, and an overtime sum written as 40 times 1,5 equals 60.
mood: Empowering and practical, workers learning their rights.
pacing: Quick restaurant tour, then the poster read line by line, a warm final line.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and know your rights before your first job.
